title: Priority: Private security regression — inconsistent RBAC/KMS audit propagation for SAML SSO customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple Private customers reported authentication failures and missing audit entries after a routine KMS rotation window. Symptom set included SSO (SAML) session invalidations, RBAC role changes not appearing in control plane UI for short intervals, and encrypted audit log entries failing to decrypt for the rotation period. The issue affected three paying customers across EU region private deployments (one on VPC, two on private on-prem bundles) and triggered an urgent escalation to Support and SE teams. Initial triage indicates a race between the RBAC sync task and the KMS rotation handler that caused partial writes of audit entries and transient invalidation of derived session signatures used by the SAML assertion verifier.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run private control plane with scheduled KMS rotation enabled (test rotation window configured per docs).
2) Simulate RBAC role update via admin API around the rotation window (roles/permissions changes to a user).
3) Observe that audit entries for the role change are written with an older key id, then a partial re-encrypt attempted with new key leading to decryption failures.
4) Simultaneously trigger SAML SSO login/refresh; the SAML validator rejects assertions when audit verification step finds missing signatures or mismatched key ids, causing session creation to fail.
5) Reproduce: occurs reliably when RBAC sync batch overlaps with KMS key rollover within ~3s window under load.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: support-run workaround — pause scheduled KMS rotations on affected customers and instruct on temporary manual rotation outside business hours.
2) Temporary fix: deploy control-plane config to retry audit-record decryption on read when key-id mismatch detected and fall back to previous key cache for up to 1 minute.
3) Communication: SE/Support notified impacted customers with recommended mitigation steps and an ETA for a permanent fix.
4) Monitoring: added on-call alert to detect >0.5% SAML login failures in private regions after a rotation event.
resolution_plan: Root cause: race condition between RBAC sync job and KMS rotation path that allowed partially updated audit records and transient signature mismatch observed by SAML validator.

1) Short-term patch (this ticket): make KMS rotation path atomic for audit writes — write new entries under new key only after full rotation completed; add strong backoff and linear retry for RBAC sync when rotation in progress.
2) SAML validator softening: make assertion verification tolerant of key-id transitions by checking both previous and current key for up to 60s during rotation window.
3) PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/12456 (KMS atomic-rotate + audit write change), github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/12457 (SAML validator tolerant lookup).
4) Tests: unit tests added for atomic rotation logic, integration tests that simulate concurrent RBAC writes during rotation, and end-to-end smoke in staging with synthetic customers.
5) Rollout: emergency patch to private control plane — canary to 2 customers in EU for 30 minutes with full observability checks; if stable, push to remaining private deployments in EU, then global.
6) Post-deploy: reprocess failed audit entries for affected window where feasible and notify customers of reprocessed/verified logs.
